anchor.quote: Limit the use of text boxes and callouts

not_rules.note: Section heading introducing broad advice on using text boxes and callouts sparingly.

anchor.quote: Don’t overuse text boxes or callouts: they become a distraction. Avoid putting content in a text box or callout just because you can’t make it fit into the flow of the text.

not_rules.note: General authorial/editorial advice without an objective standard or flaggable threshold.

anchor.quote: Before you include a text box or callout in your content, consider how it will help people understand or use the information.

not_rules.note: Mental consideration for the writer; not a text property.

anchor.quote: Text boxes should contain a summary, examples or an expansion of ideas in the body of the text.

not_rules.note: Editorial guidance on suggested content types for text boxes.

anchor.quote: Use text boxes to set information apart from the content.

covers.quote: Make it distinct from the other headings in the text so you don’t interrupt the heading hierarchy.

rules.quote: Longer text boxes should have a heading or title to show people the purpose of the text box at a glance.
rules.specification: A text box of substantial length (e.g. multiple paragraphs or over 50 words) should include a distinct heading or title.
rules.violation_condition: a longer text box without a heading or title indicating its purpose
rules.why: Specific, actionable style guidance for formatting longer text boxes (G-2).

covers.quote: Number text boxes if they feature repeatedly in content.
You can use an appropriate identifier, such as ‘Box 1’ or ‘Case study 1’.

rules.quote: Refer to numbered text boxes in the body text.
rules.violation_condition: a numbered text box that is not cross-referenced or cited in the body text
when: When text boxes are numbered because they feature repeatedly in content.
rules.why: G-2 covers the condition of numbering; body text must reference numbered boxes.

covers.quote: Make text boxes accessible in HTML
You can also use the <role=“complementary”> attribute to define an ARIA complementary landmark. Use this when it sits outside the <main> content.
Alternatively, use the <role=“region”> attribute and assign a name if the content needs to sit within the <main> section of a page.

rules.quote: For text boxes in HTML, use the <aside> element.
rules.violation_condition: a text box in HTML marked up without an <aside> element or appropriate complementary/region landmark
rules.why: Specifies structural semantic requirements for HTML text boxes; child sentences provide valid alternative ARIA attributes (G-1, G-2).

covers.quote: Don’t use text boxes in Microsoft Office documents
Instead of text boxes, use borders and paragraph styles to highlight content visually.

rules.quote: You should not use text boxes in Word and PowerPoint.
rules.violation_condition: a text box element used in a Word or PowerPoint document
when: In Microsoft Word and PowerPoint documents.
rules.why: Clear technical restriction on using native text box elements in Office files (G-1, G-4).
